entries.title: Preview as reviewer in portal loads the reviewer's Site again
entries.summary: **Preview as reviewer in portal** no longer ends in *Request Failed / Unable to load portal*. It opens the reviewer's Site, signed in as that reviewer.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers → Actions → Preview as reviewer in portal

entries.use_case: Support and organizers can see exactly what a reviewer sees while troubleshooting, without asking the reviewer for screenshots.

cs_action.note: Fix; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or CSM reports that Preview as reviewer in portal showed Request Failed or Unable to load portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer that previews reviewers' Sites while troubleshooting.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → Actions → Preview as reviewer in portal

entries.title: Sites keep working when the page is translated in the browser
entries.summary: Reviewers and applicants who use their browser's translate feature (for example Chrome Translate) no longer see *An error occurred while loading the App section* on every click. Sites now keep working when the page is translated.

where.path: Your event's Site (reviewers and applicants)

entries.use_case: Reviewers whose language the Site doesn't offer can translate the page and finish their reviews.

cs_action.note: Fix; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A reviewer or applicant reports an error loading a section after translating the page in their browser.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with reviewers or applicants whose language the Site does not offer.
internal.staff_path: Open the event's Site in a browser with page translation turned on

entries.title: Custom roles get a Restrict records switch, and Contact access is open to every event admin
entries.summary: Create Role and Edit Role now have a **Restrict records** switch for custom roles. Members of a role with it on get session filters and **Contact access** when you invite or edit them. **Contact access** is now visible to every event admin, not only Sessionboard staff.

where.path: Event Settings → Team → Roles & permissions (Create Role / Edit Role) and Event Settings → Team (invite or edit a member)

entries.use_case: Give a vendor or outside team a custom role that only sees the sessions and contacts you pick, without duplicating Session Manager first, and set the contact limits yourself instead of asking Sessionboard staff.

cs_action.note: Self-serve for every event admin; nothing to turn on. Default roles do not show the switch.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer wants a vendor or external team to see only certain sessions or contacts, or asks why Contact access was not on their invite screen.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using custom roles with limited record access, especially those with vendor or external-staff roles (e.g. Tahaluf ME event 2).
internal.staff_path: Event Settings → Team → Roles & permissions → Create Role or Edit Role
internal.gotchas: Switching Restrict records on an existing role applies to everyone who already holds it as soon as the role is saved. Default roles cannot be changed.
internal.talk_track: You can now control record restrictions directly on any custom role — no need to duplicate a built-in role. And every admin on your team can see and configure Contact access filters when inviting or editing a member.

entries.title: Sending a contract via DocuSign no longer fails when the template has no signer role
entries.summary: **Send via Docusign** no longer fails with an error when the Docusign template has no signer role. The envelope goes out to the signer you picked. If the template no longer exists in Docusign, you now see a clear message to check it and try again.

where.path: Contacts → [contact record] → Contracts → Send via DocuSign

entries.use_case: A CSM can tell a customer whose Docusign template was built without a named signer role that sending works now, and that a deleted template shows a plain message instead of a failure.

cs_action.note: Fix; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that sending a DocuSign contract returns an error or that no contract row was created after clicking Send.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the DocuSign integration with templates that have no named signer role.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → [contact record] → Contracts → Send via DocuSign
internal.gotchas: Templates with several named signer roles still send to the first one by routing order.
internal.talk_track: DocuSign templates that lacked a named signer role used to cause a 500 error and no contract record was saved. That is now fixed — Sessionboard falls back to a composite template so the envelope still goes out.

entries.title: Slack seat-request posts now include a View request link to the guest detail in Sessionboard Marketing
entries.summary: Every Slack seat-request post now includes a **View request** button that opens the guest's full detail in Sessionboard Marketing — showing form answers, organization, other requests from the same company, and who made the decision. Once a request is decided, the decision buttons are replaced by an inline note ("Approved by … in Sessionboard · date · **View request**"). Existing open posts are refreshed in place so they pick up the button without a second message.

where.path: Events → an in-person event → Guests; Slack seat-request channel

entries.use_case: Approvers who receive seat-request notifications in Slack can jump straight to the full guest record in Sessionboard Marketing — seeing all form answers, the requester's organization, and other pending requests from the same company — without hunting for the record manually.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses Slack seat-request approvals for in-person events and wants approvers to have more context before deciding.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person field events with Slack approvals enabled.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → an in-person event → Guests; Settings → Slack approvals
internal.gotchas: Existing open Slack posts are refreshed in place (chat.update) to add the button — no duplicate messages are sent. The link click is silently acknowledged on the Slack side.
internal.talk_track: Approvers can now click View request right in Slack to see the full guest record — answers, company, and other pending requests from the same org — before they approve or decline.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the View request button on Slack posts, the guest detail drawer (form answers labelled with questions, organization, other requests from the same org, decision audit), and the in-place post refresh behaviour for existing open requests.
draft.why_use_it: Slack seat-request approvals let your team decide who gets a seat at a field event without leaving Slack. Each post shows the requester's details and gives approvers **Approve**, **Waitlist** and **Decline** buttons; decisions are recorded with the approver's name, timestamp and whether they acted in Slack or Sessionboard. The **View request** link opens the full guest record so approvers can check form answers, see the requester's organization, and review other pending requests from the same company before deciding.

entries.title: Slack app card now lists seat approvals alongside team kits
entries.summary: The Slack app card in **Apps** now shows two capability chips: **Seat approvals** (in-person seat requests with Approve / Waitlist / Decline buttons posted to a channel) and **Team kits as Slack DMs**. The card description also updates to "Seat requests to approve in a channel, and team kits as Slack DMs."

where.path: Marketing → Apps → Slack

entries.use_case: Organizers checking the Slack app card can now see at a glance that it handles both seat-request approvals and team kit DMs, so they know what to expect before connecting Slack.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks what the Slack integration does or is confused about whether seat approvals work in Slack.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running in-person events who use Slack for approvals.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Apps → Slack
internal.gotchas: This PR only fixes the UI label; the underlying seat-approval functionality shipped in web-api #5569.
internal.talk_track: The Slack card now accurately shows both things it does: approve seat requests right in a Slack channel, and receive team kit DMs.

draft.docs_gap: The /sessionboard-marketing/apps guide should document the Slack app's two capabilities: seat-request approvals in a channel and team kit DMs.

entries.title: Reply by email for event requests, approvals, file requests, CRM and marketing sends
entries.summary: Emails sent for event requests, approval reviews, file-request revisions, CRM native sends (invite to speak, nominate), and marketing newsletters and journeys now include a reply line. Replying to an event-request email threads the response back to the request. Replying to an approval email with **Approve** or **Deny**/**Reject** (plus an optional note) records the decision as the reviewer. Replying to a "needs changes" file-request email with an attachment submits a new pending revision through the portal. Replies to CRM and marketing sends are recorded on the contact's timeline as "Replied to <subject>" and the sender is notified. Unrecognised senders are held; quoted text and signatures are stripped automatically.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reply by Email; replies then appear in the relevant request, approval, file request, or contact timeline automatically

where.path: Event Requests; Approvals; Portals → file requests; CRM contacts timeline; Marketing contacts timeline

entries.use_case: Teams that manage event requests, approvals, or file collection can let reviewers and contacts respond directly from their inbox without logging in. Reviewers can approve or deny a submission with a one-word reply, and speakers can submit a revised file by replying to the "needs changes" email.

cs_action.note: Controlled by the REPLY_BY_EMAIL_CRM_ENABLED flag (off by default). Can be scoped to specific org IDs via REPLY_BY_EMAIL_CRM_ORG_IDS. Requires support or CSM to enable per org.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks reviewers or speakers to act on emails without logging in, or when approval turnaround is slow because reviewers don't open Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with active approval workflows, file-request workflows, or CRM/marketing sends who want faster response rates from reviewers and speakers.
internal.staff_path: Flag: REPLY_BY_EMAIL_CRM_ENABLED (optional REPLY_BY_EMAIL_CRM_ORG_IDS)
internal.gotchas: Only the original recipient's email (or a linked contact email) is accepted; anyone else is held. Designed (GrapesJS) emails do not get the reply line. Transactional emails and digests are untouched. File replies go through the portal's own upload handler — deadline, access, file deny-list and SVG checks all apply. Approval replies only work while the reviewer is pending on the current step.
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers can approve or deny a submission by replying to the email with a single word. Speakers can send a revised file by replying to the 'needs changes' email. Every reply lands on the right record automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the reply-by-email capability: what surfaces support it, how to reply to approve/deny, how to submit a file revision by reply, and how replies appear on the CRM and marketing contact timeline.
draft.why_use_it: Reply by email lets organizers, reviewers, and participants act on Sessionboard notifications without opening the platform. Reviewers approve or deny submissions from their inbox, speakers submit revised files by replying with an attachment, and contacts' email replies are automatically threaded back to the right record. Every reply is verified against the recipient's address so only the intended person's response is accepted.

entries.title: Reply to a Messages notification email to post directly into the thread
entries.summary: When enabled, replying to a **message.new** or **message.mention** notification email posts the reply into the conversation thread — no need to open Sessionboard. Quoted text and signatures are stripped automatically. Works for team, speaker portal, and reviewer messaging; internal-note emails reply as internal notes. Replies from unrecognised senders are held and never posted.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reply by Email; then messages arrive with a reply address at replies.sessionboard.com

where.path: Messages notification emails (reply directly from your email client)

entries.use_case: Teams and speakers who live in their inbox can keep a conversation moving without switching to Sessionboard — a reply to the notification email lands in the thread just like a message sent from the app.

cs_action.note: Requires REPLY_BY_EMAIL_MESSAGES_ENABLED=true per region, plus SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_SECRET and the Inbound Parse URL configured. ME region stores replies but holds them as unverified until the parse secret is set. An optional REPLY_ADDRESS_SECRET should be set before the flag goes on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks for a faster way for speakers or team members to respond to messages without logging in, or when inbox-first workflows are important.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with active messaging workflows — especially those coordinating with many speakers or reviewers who are slow to log in.
internal.gotchas: Only immediate message.new and message.mention emails are reply-enabled; digest emails are not. Replies from addresses not linked to the recipient's account are silently held (held_sender) and never posted. ME region replies are held until SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_SECRET is configured. The flag can be scoped to specific org IDs via REPLY_BY_EMAIL_MESSAGES_ORG_IDS for a pilot rollout.
internal.talk_track: Your speakers and reviewers can now reply to message notifications straight from their inbox — the reply lands in the thread, quoted text stripped, and only people who still have access can post.

draft.docs_gap: The notifications and messaging guide should add a section explaining reply-by-email: how the reply address works, which email types support it, how sender verification works, and what happens when access is lost or a sender is unrecognised.
draft.why_use_it: Messages lets organizers, speakers, and reviewers exchange notes inside Sessionboard without leaving the platform context. With reply-by-email, every notification email becomes a two-way channel: recipients answer from their inbox and the reply appears in the thread for everyone involved. Quoted text and signatures are stripped so the thread stays clean, and access rules are re-checked at reply time so only authorised participants can post.

entries.title: Replies to campaign, Send Email and decision emails are saved to Communications history
entries.summary: When a contact replies to a **Send Email**, an email campaign, or a Sessions decision email, the reply is stored on that contact's **Communications** history as a response. The original sender receives a **email.reply_received** notification (bell and email). Replies from unrecognised senders are held rather than stored. A copy is forwarded to the configured branded Reply-To address.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Reply by Email for admin sends; replies then appear automatically in Communications → History

where.path: Communications → History (Emails tab) → a sent email → Responses

entries.use_case: Teams that send decision emails or campaigns and need to track speaker or contact replies without checking a separate inbox can see every reply threaded directly on the original email in Communications history.

cs_action.note: Feature is behind REPLY_BY_EMAIL_ADMIN_SENDS_ENABLED (default off). Enable per org via the flag or REPLY_BY_EMAIL_ADMIN_SENDS_ORG_IDS. Requires INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN and Inbound Parse secret to be configured on the API server.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why speaker or contact replies to campaigns or decision emails don't appear in Sessionboard, or when they want a full conversation thread on a contact record.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who actively use Send Email, email campaigns or Sessions decision emails and want replies captured in Communications history.
internal.staff_path: Communications → History → a sent email → Responses
internal.gotchas: Newsletters, journeys, lifecycle and Advocacy sends are excluded. Decision emails only participate when reply-to-complete is off. Replies from unrecognised senders are held (status: held_sender) and not stored. The mint step is fail-open — if it fails, the email goes out with the original Reply-To and no reply address is written.
internal.talk_track: Replies to your campaign and decision emails now land directly on the contact's Communications history, so your team sees the full conversation without leaving Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The History guide should document the Responses sub-section on a sent email, the held_sender status, and the email.reply_received notification type introduced by this feature.
draft.why_use_it: The Communications history gives you a complete record of every email exchanged with a contact or speaker, including their replies, all in one place. When a contact replies to a campaign, a Send Email, or a session decision email, the reply is stored alongside the original message so your team never loses context. The original sender is notified immediately, and a copy is forwarded to your branded inbox so existing workflows are not disrupted. Replies from addresses not linked to the recipient are held automatically, keeping the record clean.

entries.title: See a requester's email replies on Event Requests
entries.summary: When a requester replies to a confirmation, ready, or declined email for an event request, their reply now appears in a **Replies by email** section on the request record — showing the sender, timestamp, message text, and any attached file links.

where.path: Event Requests → a request record → Replies by email

entries.use_case: Organizers who send confirmation or status emails for event requests can now read a requester's reply directly on the request record, without digging through a shared inbox — keeping the full conversation in one place.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to track back-and-forth with requesters after sending confirmation or declined emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Event Requests who sends status emails and needs to track requester replies.
internal.staff_path: Event Requests → open a request → Replies by email
internal.gotchas: A copy of each reply also goes to the success inbox. The section is hidden when there are no replies, so it will not appear on older requests that predate the feature.
internal.talk_track: Replies from requesters now show up right on the request record — sender, time, message and any files — so you never have to hunt through your inbox to find what they said.

draft.docs_gap: The automated-emails guide should document the Replies by email section on event request records, including what triggers a reply to be captured and where it appears.
draft.why_use_it: Event Requests lets organizers manage inbound requests and communicate status changes by email. The Replies by email section keeps the requester's responses attached to the request record so the whole conversation — original request, status decision, and any follow-up from the requester — is visible in one place without switching to an email client.

entries.title: Media: see every untagged voice and recording at a glance, then tag them all at once
entries.summary: A new **Speakers to tag** view lists every recording that has an unnamed voice or no linked session, with talk-time stats, sample transcript lines, and ranked speaker suggestions. Select the right person (or mark a voice as not a speaker) across up to 200 recordings and apply all assignments in one step.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Speakers to tag

entries.use_case: Organizers with many recordings can find every unnamed voice across all recordings in one place, review AI-ranked suggestions with confidence scores, and resolve all tagging gaps in a single bulk action instead of opening each recording individually.

cs_action.note: The PR notes the endpoint was not run end-to-end against a live database (only read-only SQL against a replica). Confirm the UI PR on the same branch is also merged and the feature is stable before surfacing to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has many recordings with unresolved voices or missing session links and is blocked from generating clips or quotes.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Media (add-on) with a high volume of recordings, especially post-event when transcription is complete.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Speakers to tag
internal.gotchas: Voices with less than 30 seconds of talk time are hidden from the list and counted only in a summary badge. Portfolio and event-only staff see only recordings scoped to their events; org-wide session suggestions are available only to org-level staff. The bulk apply endpoint accepts a maximum of 200 assignments per call.
internal.talk_track: Instead of opening 36 recordings one by one to find unnamed voices, open Speakers to tag, review the AI suggestions, and tag everyone in one click.

draft.docs_gap: The media-library guide should add a section explaining the Speakers to tag view: how to read the voice list, what the confidence scores mean, and how to use bulk apply.
draft.why_use_it: Media turns recordings into clips, quotes and recaps — but only after each voice is linked to a speaker. The Speakers to tag view surfaces every recording with an unnamed voice or a missing session link, shows how much each voice spoke, plays sample audio, and ranks the most likely speakers by name, identity history and session schedule. Resolving all gaps at once keeps your content pipeline moving without manual recording-by-recording review.

entries.title: Blind review now hides company, job title, affiliations and identifying custom fields
entries.summary: When a review round has blind review enabled, the reviewer payload no longer exposes **Company**, **Job Title**, past companies, educational affiliation, bio (**About**), avatar, website, social links (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook), street address, honorific, or salutation. Custom fields of type email or phone, and any custom field whose label contains words such as "company", "organisation", "employer", "affiliation", "job title" or "LinkedIn", are also hidden. City, state and country remain visible so reviewers can make travel-support decisions; admins can mark those fields sensitive if needed.

enable.path: Program → Review Plans → a plan → Rounds → a round → enable Blind Review

where.path: Program → Review Plans → a plan → reviewer evaluation view

entries.use_case: Programmes with at-risk or anonymised applicants can now trust that blind review truly hides every identifying detail — not just name and email — so reviewers score on merit alone.

cs_action.note: Any customer who previously relied on blind review for at-risk applicants (e.g. medical, legal, or advocacy programmes) should be told that company, job title, affiliations, social links and identifying custom fields are now also hidden. Confirm they do not need city/state/country hidden too — if so, advise marking those fields sensitive.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about blind review, runs a programme with vulnerable or anonymous applicants, or reports that reviewer payloads were leaking company or job title data.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event using blind review on an application form, especially programmes in healthcare, legal, advocacy or diversity contexts.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review Plans → a plan → Rounds → a round → Blind Review toggle
internal.gotchas: City, state and country are intentionally left visible for travel-support decisions. Custom fields are hidden by label match — any field whose label merely contains a flagged word (e.g. 'organisation') will be hidden. Session (non-application) blind review is unchanged by this PR and still only hides name/email/phones.
internal.talk_track: Blind review now hides everything that could identify an applicant — company, title, affiliations, social profiles and any custom field labelled with those words — so your committee scores on merit alone.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the full list of standard and custom fields hidden under blind review, note that city/state/country remain visible by default, and explain how admins can mark additional fields sensitive.
draft.why_use_it: Blind review lets your committee score submissions without knowing who submitted them, reducing unconscious bias and protecting applicant privacy. When blind review is on, the reviewer scorecard strips all contact-identifying information from the submission view so scores reflect the work, not the person. Admins control which fields are visible to reviewers and can mark additional fields as sensitive for programmes with stricter anonymity requirements.

entries.title: Blind review now hides applicant company, job title and other identifying answers
entries.summary: When a review round has **Blind Review** enabled, the reviewer portal no longer displays the applicant's company, job title, or any answer whose field type or label identifies the person — including name, email, phone, organisation, employer, affiliation, LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, website and address fields.

enable.path: Review Plans → a plan → Rounds → a round → Blind Review

where.path: Reviewer portal → a submission under review

entries.use_case: Organisations running blind review to reduce bias can now trust that reviewers will not see company, job title or other identifying details — even if those answers are present in the submission payload.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that reviewers could still see applicant company or job title under blind review, or when setting up a blind review round.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using blind review rounds in their evaluation plans.
internal.staff_path: Review Plans → a plan → Rounds → a round → Blind Review (toggle on)
internal.gotchas: The portal-side label matching is intentionally broader than the API filter — it also suppresses 'title', 'website' and 'address' fields. This is the safe failure direction under blind review.
internal.talk_track: Blind review now fully hides company, job title and all other identifying fields in the reviewer portal, so your reviewers score on content alone.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note which specific field labels and answer types are hidden from reviewers when Blind Review is active (name, email, phone, company, organisation, employer, affiliation, job title, title, LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, website, address, and email- or phone-typed custom fields).
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Reviewer portal shows application answers and applicant context
entries.summary: When a review subject is an application, the reviewer portal now shows an **Answers** section listing the applicant's form responses (sensitive fields are hidden), and a **This applicant at [event]** panel showing their sessions and roles. Under blind review, only counts appear ("Speaker on 2 sessions · Moderator on 1") with a "Names hidden: blind review" notice. The heading reads **Application** instead of the shadow row title.

where.path: Reviewer portal → My Reviews → a submission detail view

entries.use_case: Reviewers evaluating applications can read the applicant's form answers and see their existing program involvement — sessions and roles — without leaving the review portal, giving them the context they need to score fairly. Blind review mode keeps names hidden while still surfacing participation counts.

cs_action.note: Requires the appreview-api web-api branch to be live; the applicant context panel only appears when the API returns applicantContext. Confirm with engineering before surfacing to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses Applications and wants reviewers to evaluate applicants with program context, or when they ask about blind review for applications.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running application-based review programs (awards, grants, fellowships) who want reviewers to see applicant history.
internal.staff_path: Reviewer portal → My Reviews → open an application submission
internal.gotchas: The applicant context panel is hidden if the API does not return applicantContext. eventName falls back to 'this event' if not provided. Sensitive fields are dropped both client-side and by the API.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers now see the applicant's answers and their existing role on the program right in the review portal — and if you run blind review, they only see participation counts, not names.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the application review view in the reviewer portal, including the Answers section, the applicant context panel, and how blind review affects what is shown.
draft.why_use_it: The reviewer portal gives committee members everything they need to score a submission in one place. Application review extends this to show the applicant's own answers alongside their event history, so reviewers can weigh both the proposal and the person's track record. Blind review mode surfaces participation counts without revealing names, keeping the process impartial when that matters.

entries.title: Review applications: score, decide and notify applicants from an application form
entries.summary: Application forms can now have a full review plan attached. Organizers create a plan on the form, assign reviewers to rounds, score submissions, record **Accept** or **Decline** decisions with an optional amount awarded and funding kind, and send decision emails — all without leaving the Applications module. The submissions list gains **Review Round**, **Review Score**, **Amount Awarded** and **Funding Kind** columns that are sortable, filterable and exportable. Reviewers see application answers (sensitive fields hidden; names and contact details hidden under blind review) in the reviewer portal. Applicants see their decision status and, once accepted, any amount awarded on the public form. An **Audit Log** records every form edit, plan change, decision and decision email. AI review is off by default on application plans.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the applications_review flag; then Applications → Forms → a form → Review

where.path: Applications → Forms → a form → Review; Applications → Forms → a form → Submissions

entries.use_case: Teams that collect applications — grants, scholarships, speaking slots, membership — can run a structured multi-round review and send accept/decline emails with award amounts directly from the application form, without needing a separate workflow.

cs_action.note: Requires the applications_review event flag to be turned on by support or CSM. Every new route returns 404 without it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer uses application forms for grants, scholarships, fellowships or any selection process that needs a scored review committee and formal accept/decline communications.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using Applications who need a committee review step — associations, foundations, academic conferences, grant programs.
internal.staff_path: Applications → Forms → a form → Review (tab appears once flag is on)
internal.gotchas: AI review is disabled by default on application plans (ai_review_enabled = false); Screener personas and AI feedback summaries will return errors until AI review is explicitly turned on. Shadow session rows are created for each submission but are intentionally hidden from Program › Review lists. Deleting a submission detaches but does not delete its review history. The reviewer search list does not yet surface application-specific fields.
internal.talk_track: You already collect applications through the form — now you can run a full scored review, track decisions and send accept/decline emails with award amounts, all in the same place, with a complete audit trail.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document how to attach a review plan to an application form, the sensitive-field and blind-review settings, how to record and send decisions with amounts awarded, what applicants see on the public form after a decision, and the audit log.
draft.why_use_it: Application Review brings the same structured, multi-round scoring workflow used for session submissions to application forms. Organizers set up rounds, assign reviewers, define scorecards and track progress through a monitor — all scoped to a single form. Decisions, amounts awarded and decision emails are recorded per submission, and every change is captured in an audit log so the process is fully traceable. Reviewers work through a dedicated portal that respects blind-review and sensitive-field settings, keeping applicant privacy intact throughout.

entries.title: Application forms can now collect and link attendee registrations
entries.summary: A new **Attendee** form type lets organizers build application forms that write answers directly onto a registrant's record. When a signed-in attendee submits, their registration is matched by account or email and updated in one step; unmatched submissions are linked automatically when the registration arrives later. The submissions list gains **Registration status** and **Attendee email** columns. Existing **Contact** forms are unchanged.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Attendee application forms; then Events → [event] → Applications → Forms → New Form → Type: Attendee

where.path: Events → [event] → Applications → Forms

entries.use_case: Use this when you want to collect additional information from registered attendees — such as dietary needs, session preferences or compliance answers — and have those answers land directly on their registration record without any manual data entry.

cs_action.note: Requires the staff-only event flag `applications_review` AND the org Attendees setting (`flag_enable_attendees`) to be on. Both are off by default and cannot be self-served.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to collect post-registration information from attendees and write it back to the registration record, or when they want a form that targets registrants rather than speakers or contacts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run registration and want to collect supplemental attendee data (dietary, compliance, session preferences) without a separate tool.
internal.staff_path: Enable `applications_review` event flag + `flag_enable_attendees` org setting; then Events → [event] → Applications → Forms → New Form → Type: Attendee
internal.gotchas: Form type is fixed at creation — it cannot be changed after the form is saved. Attendee forms accept only attendee-module fields; contact/system fields (e.g. Status) are rejected. The public submit route now requires a Bearer token (401 without one). Email answers are never written onto the registration's identity email. Saved-view filters and sorts are not yet applied to attendee submission lists. The `reviewEnabled` / `reviewPlanId` fields on form rows are deferred to a follow-up PR (SB-11623).
internal.talk_track: If you collect extra information from attendees after they register — dietary needs, session preferences, compliance questions — an Attendee application form writes those answers straight onto the registration record the moment someone submits, and catches up automatically for anyone who submits before their registration is created.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the new Attendee form type: how to create one, the required starter fields (First/Last name, Email, Company, Job title), how registration matching works, the deferred-link behaviour, and the Registration status and Attendee email columns in the submissions list.
draft.why_use_it: Application forms let you gather structured information from people before, during or after an event and review it in one place. The Attendee form type connects those answers to the registration record automatically, so the data your team collects is always tied to the right person. Submissions that arrive before a registration is created are held and linked as soon as the registration appears, so no answers are lost. The submissions list shows registration status alongside each response, giving your team a clear picture of who has registered and who has not.

entries.title: Attendees list and Attendee fields tab available without Pathways
entries.summary: When the **Attendees** setting is on, **CRM → People → Attendees** shows the full attendee list without requiring Pathways, and a new **Attendee** tab appears in **Library → Fields** so organizers can manage attendee-specific fields in one place. With the setting off, the Pathways upsell is shown instead and the **Attendee** tab is hidden.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Attendees; then Settings → Admin → Attendees

where.path: CRM → People → Attendees; Library → Fields → Attendee tab

entries.use_case: Organizations that track event attendees in Sessionboard but have not purchased Pathways can now view the attendee list and manage attendee fields directly, without needing to enable the full Pathways add-on.

cs_action.note: The org-level `flag_enable_attendees` flag must be turned on by a super-user via Settings → Admin or the API before the CRM Attendees list and Attendee fields tab appear. This is not self-serve.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to view or manage attendees in the CRM but does not have Pathways, or asks why the Attendees menu item is missing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Application Review phase 2 rollout who need attendee visibility without the full Pathways add-on.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Admin → Attendees (super-user only); then CRM → People → Attendees and Library → Fields → Attendee tab
internal.gotchas: The Admin toggle is on a super-user-only page; local super-user creation is blocked by a DB trigger in some environments. Pathways-specific UI (Early Access badge, Program report, Pre-event quiz, Person 360 row click) is hidden when Pathways is off even if the Attendees setting is on. The old `/settings/attendee-fields` route redirects to `Library → Fields?module=attendees` when the setting is on; field-event orgs still reach it from the registration form editor when the setting is off.
internal.talk_track: You can now see your full attendee list and manage attendee fields right in the CRM — no Pathways subscription required. Just ask us to flip the switch.

draft.docs_gap: The Pathways overview guide should document the standalone Attendees setting (flag_enable_attendees), explain what becomes available without Pathways, and note which Pathways-only features (Program report, Pre-event quiz, Person 360) remain hidden until Pathways is enabled.
draft.why_use_it: Pathways gives you a unified view of every person who attends your events, letting you track engagement, build segments, and understand how attendees move through your program over time. The Attendees list surfaces all registered participants in one place so your team can act on attendance data without switching tools. Attendee fields let you capture and organize the information that matters most for your audience — from dietary preferences to session interests — and reuse those fields across events.

entries.title: New org setting unlocks CRM › People › Attendees without Pathways
entries.summary: A new **Enable Attendees** setting on an organization lets every event user see **CRM › People › Attendees** without requiring a Pathways subscription. When the setting is off, the nav item remains staff-only, exactly as before.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Attendees; then CRM → People → Attendees

where.path: CRM → People → Attendees

entries.use_case: Organizations that track attendee engagement but do not have Pathways can now surface the Attendees list in CRM without upgrading their subscription tier.

cs_action.note: The org-level flag `flag_enable_attendees` defaults to false; a PUT to /organizations/:orgId with enableAttendees: true is required, or ask engineering to flip it. No UI toggle exists yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a non-Pathways customer asks why they cannot see attendees in CRM, or when a customer wants to cross-reference attendees with their speaker/contact records.
internal.who_should_get_it: Orgs that collect attendee data (via registration integrations or imports) but do not have Pathways.
internal.staff_path: CRM → People → Attendees (visible only after the flag is on)
internal.gotchas: The flag is org-level only for now; it shows the nav item for every event user in that org. The attendee list endpoint was already permission-gated, so enabling the nav does not bypass existing data permissions.
internal.talk_track: Turn on Attendees in CRM so your team can see who came to each event right alongside your speakers and contacts — no Pathways required.

draft.docs_gap: The Speaker CRM overview guide should document the Enable Attendees org setting and explain that CRM › People › Attendees is available without Pathways when the setting is on.
draft.why_use_it: The Attendees view in CRM › People gives organizers a single place to see everyone who attended their events alongside speaker and contact records. Use it to follow up with attendees, build segments, or understand who is engaging across your program without switching tools.

entries.title: Sites now support 29 UI languages, including Arabic and Hebrew (RTL)
entries.summary: The language menu on Sites (reviewer, applicant and auth flows) now offers 29 languages — up from 4 — including **Português (Brasil)**, **العربية**, **עברית**, **日本語**, **中文 (繁體)**, **中文 (简体)**, **한국어**, **हिन्दी**, **ภาษาไทย** and 20 more. Arabic and Hebrew pages render fully right-to-left, with labels, icons and tab order mirrored. The browser's language setting and the `?lng=` preview parameter both resolve to the correct catalog automatically.

where.path: Sites → Site builder → language menu (bottom of the page)

entries.use_case: Events with Brazilian, Arabic-speaking, Hebrew-speaking, Japanese, Korean, or other non-Western-European reviewers and speakers no longer fall back to browser auto-translate. Participants see the Site in their browser's language automatically, and organizers can preview any language from the builder.

cs_action.note: Ships on by default; no flag to flip. Catalogs were machine-translated by DeepL; only Portuguese (Brazilian) has had a human review pass. No native-speaker review has been done for the other 24 new languages.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has reviewers, speakers or applicants whose primary language is not English, French, Spanish or German — especially Brazilian Portuguese, Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Hindi or Southeast Asian languages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running international CFPs, awards or reviewer programs with non-Western-European audiences.
internal.staff_path: Sites → Site builder → language menu
internal.gotchas: Only the 24 new catalogs beyond pt have not been reviewed by a native speaker; customers who notice translation errors should report them to Sessionboard Support. RTL layout was not verified on the reviewer scoring screens, checkout, Content Gallery, Learning, FloorMap, EventPage or Vote — those are a follow-up. Thai text may break mid-word rather than overflow.
internal.talk_track: If your Brazilian reviewers or Arabic-speaking speakers have been relying on Chrome Translate to read the portal, they will now see a fully translated interface automatically — including a right-to-left layout for Arabic and Hebrew.

draft.docs_gap: The Site builder guide should document the language menu, how the browser language is detected and mapped (including pt-BR → pt, zh-TW → zh-Hant, no/nn → nb), how to preview a language with ?lng= in the builder, and which areas of the Site do not yet have RTL layout (Content Gallery, Learning, FloorMap, EventPage, Vote).
draft.why_use_it: Sites automatically serve the interface in the visitor's browser language, so reviewers, speakers and applicants read instructions, labels and navigation in their own language without any extra setup. Right-to-left support for Arabic and Hebrew means the full page — layout, icons, tab order and form fields — mirrors correctly. Organizers can preview any of the 29 languages directly from the Site builder using the `?lng=` parameter.

entries.title: Clip sharing share count, email tile layout, speaker tagging confidence and Discover source links corrected
entries.summary: Four fixes from an end-to-end review of clip sharing: the **Shared** count now reflects only share actions (not views, downloads or copies); share email tiles use a consistent size and pick a tall, wide or square crop based on the aspect ratios of the moments included; a voice saved under a suggested contact's exact name is now shown as a high-confidence **Speakers to tag** suggestion, while a suggestion that contradicts the typed name is capped at 30% so **Accept all high-confidence** never applies it; and every **Discover** result now carries a direct link to the provider's own page when one is available.

where.path: Marketing → Clips

entries.use_case: Organizers who share clips with advocates can now trust that the Shared count reflects actual shares, that email tiles look polished regardless of clip orientation, and that the Speakers to tag suggestions correctly promote or suppress candidates based on name matching — reducing manual review time.

cs_action.note: All four are bug fixes; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their Shared count looks inflated, that clip share emails have mismatched image sizes, that a wrong speaker is being suggested at high confidence, or that Discover results have no source link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips, Speakers to tag or Discover.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips → share a clip; Marketing → Clips → Speakers to tag
internal.gotchas: The square (mixed-orientation) email tile shape and the Discover source link were not verified in a browser during QA — only the share count and speaker confidence fixes were confirmed visually.
internal.talk_track: The Shared count on a clip now only counts actual share actions, so the number you see matches what advocates actually did. Speaker tagging is smarter: an exact name match jumps to high confidence, and a conflicting name is held at 30% so bulk-accept never applies a wrong suggestion.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the Speakers to tag confidence tiers (high/medium/low), what triggers each level, and how Accept all high-confidence works.
draft.why_use_it: Clips lets you cut the best moments from session recordings and share them with speakers, advocates and your audience. You can create audiograms, distribute clips through advocacy campaigns, and track how each clip performs. The Speakers to tag feature surfaces the right people to credit on each clip, and Discover helps you find relevant content across connected sources.

entries.title: Clip share wizard sends the exact sizes chosen, and the share page gains grouping, badges and cleaner previews
entries.summary: **Share wizard** now sends only the render sizes that were selected — previously, choosing sizes for a clip with a single render was ignored and every available size was added back by the server (a 3-clip share recorded 12 renders; it now records 3). The **share page** opens with one gallery and a **Group** switch (**All together**, **Session**, **Date shared**); cards show their session name, and the newest clips carry a **New** badge. The clip preview no longer draws a duplicate logo, name or frame over clips that already contain them. **Download** and **Instagram** buttons show a loading state while the clip is fetched, and a dead share link reports the error immediately instead of spinning for ~8 seconds. In **Speakers to tag**, long recording names wrap instead of overflowing into the Voice column, and an unknown talk time shows a dash rather than "0 sec". In **Discover**, a file's name opens it in its source in a new tab when the source has a page.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips

entries.use_case: Organizers sharing clips with speakers, sponsors or attendees will now get exactly the render sizes they chose — no surprise extras — and recipients land on a cleaner share page that groups clips by session or date and highlights what is new.

cs_action.note: All fixes ship automatically; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that clip shares contained more render sizes than they selected, or that the share page looked cluttered or showed duplicate branding on previews.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips to share session recordings with speakers or sponsors.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share
internal.gotchas: The API branch fix/clip-share-walkthrough must be released first (lennd/sessionboard-web-api); the UI reads source_url from it but degrades gracefully without it.
internal.talk_track: The share wizard now sends exactly the sizes you pick — no more phantom renders — and the share page is cleaner with grouping, New badges and proper loading states on Download and Instagram.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the share-page Group switch (All together / Session / Date shared), the New badge on recent clips, and the Speakers to tag and Discover surfaces within Media.
draft.why_use_it: Clips lets you cut short, shareable video moments from session recordings and send personalised share links to speakers, sponsors and attendees. Each recipient gets a branded page where they can preview, download or post their clip directly to social channels. Use it to extend the reach of your event content without any video editing expertise.

entries.title: Share clips without sending an email and get each person's private gallery link
entries.summary: When sharing clips through the clip-share wizard, organizers can now turn off the automated email and instead receive each recipient's private gallery link to distribute themselves. **Media History** records whether a share was sent by email or delivered as a link, so the audit trail stays accurate either way.

where.path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share

entries.use_case: Useful when an organizer wants to paste each speaker's private clip link into a personal email, Slack message, or CRM follow-up rather than having Sessionboard send the notification automatically. Also covers situations where the sending domain is not yet configured or the organizer simply prefers to control the outreach themselves.

cs_action.note: Default-on improvement to the existing clip-share wizard; no enablement needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to share clips without triggering an automated email, or wants to paste individual links into their own outreach tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips who manages their own speaker or sponsor communications outside Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Clips → Share
internal.gotchas: People with no email address on file are still skipped even when email is turned off — the link-only path does not bypass that requirement.
internal.talk_track: You can now grab each person's private gallery link from the share wizard and drop it into your own email or CRM, without Sessionboard sending anything automatically.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the email-optional toggle and the returned per-person link list in the share wizard, and note that Media History distinguishes email shares from link shares.
draft.why_use_it: Clips lets you cut short, shareable video moments from session recordings and send each speaker or sponsor contact a private gallery link to their own content. You control who gets which clip, and recipients see only their own material. Use it to give speakers ready-made social content right after the event, or to deliver sponsor highlight reels as part of a post-event report.

entries.title: Copy individual share links from the clip share wizard without sending email
entries.summary: The clip share wizard's new **Delivery** step lets organizers choose **Email each person**, **Give me their share links**, or both. When links are requested, the wizard stays open after sending and lists each person's private link with **Copy**, **Copy all**, and **Download CSV** options. When email is turned off, the subject, From address, message, preview, and test button are hidden and the action button reads **Create links for N people** or **Share with N people**.

where.path: Marketing → Clips → Share → Delivery

entries.use_case: Organizers who manage their own outreach channels — or who want to paste links into a Slack message, a sponsor email, or a registration platform — can now grab every person's private clip link in one step without triggering a Sessionboard email.

cs_action.note: Default-on improvement to the existing share wizard; no flag to flip.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to distribute clip links through their own email tool, CRM, or registration platform instead of sending from Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Clips who manages speaker or sponsor communications outside Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Clips → Share → Delivery
internal.gotchas: Requires the API change in lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5602 to be deployed first; without it the wizard still emails and returns no links.
internal.talk_track: You can now grab every person's private clip link as a CSV and drop them into your own email tool or CRM — no Sessionboard email required.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the new Delivery step, the link-list screen (Copy, Copy all, Download CSV), and the email-off flow.
draft.why_use_it: Clips lets you cut short, shareable video moments from session recordings and send each speaker, sponsor, or attendee a personalised link to their own clip. Because each link is private to that person, they can post it to LinkedIn or embed it on their site knowing it reflects their contribution. Use Clips when you want to turn a single recording into a wave of authentic social posts without manually editing dozens of videos.

entries.title: Pick jobs across five products, see the cost, and sign up in one step
entries.summary: A new **/get-started** page lets prospective customers choose the jobs they want — 16 options across Program, CRM, Marketing, Publish and Learning — watch the cost build in a live sidebar (or bottom sheet on mobile), then create an account and activate every chosen product in a single sign-up flow. Deep-link URLs such as `?jobs=advocacy,call-for-speakers` pre-select cards, and picks survive a page refresh or a Back navigation from the sign-up step.

where.path: /get-started (public, pre-login)

entries.use_case: When a prospect wants more than one Sessionboard product, they can pick every job they need on a single page, see exactly what each product costs and what the 14-day trial covers, and start everything at once — instead of signing up for each product separately.

cs_action.note: Public self-serve page; no staff action required. The site's 'Get started' buttons will be pointed at /get-started in a follow-up growth-pages PR once the route is live in production.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or new customer asks how to try multiple Sessionboard products at once, or when a CSM is onboarding someone who wants Sessions plus Marketing (or any multi-product combination).
internal.who_should_get_it: Any prospective customer evaluating more than one Sessionboard product.
internal.staff_path: /get-started
internal.gotchas: Marketing-only picks redirect to Marketing's own sign-up (/signup/marketing); only the first pick is carried as the focus and other Marketing picks are not auto-enabled. Someone already signed in sees a note pointing to their workspace's product menu — adding picks to an existing workspace from this page is not yet built. Prices shown are Starter plan prices; trials run on Growth limits. Strings for ar, de, es and fr fall back to English.
internal.talk_track: You can go to /get-started, tick every job you want — call for speakers, CRM, advocacy, courses, whatever — watch the price add up, and start all of it with one sign-up. Each product gets its own 14-day free trial from today.

draft.docs_gap: The /get-started/overview guide should document the /get-started picker page: how to select jobs, read the cost sidebar, use deep-link URLs to pre-select cards, and what happens during the combined sign-up for multiple products.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard spans program management, CRM, marketing, learning and awards. The Get started page lets you browse all 16 jobs across those products, build a shortlist, and see the combined cost before you commit. One sign-up creates your account and activates every product you chose, each starting its own 14-day free trial. You land directly on the first job you picked, so you can get to work immediately.

entries.title: LinkedIn connect completes reliably when the sign-in pop-up loses its opener
entries.summary: Connecting LinkedIn on a clip share page, **Post to LinkedIn** card, or speaker verification no longer silently stalls after signing in. When LinkedIn's sign-in pages break the pop-up's link back to the starting page, the callback now routes the authorisation code through a **BroadcastChannel** so the connection still completes. Cancelling or declining on LinkedIn's consent screen now shows a clear cancellation message instead of nothing.

where.path: Marketing → Advocacy → clip share page / Post to LinkedIn card / speaker verification → Connect LinkedIn

entries.use_case: Speakers and participants who click Connect LinkedIn and sign in through LinkedIn's own login page will now see their connection complete and the button change to "Post to LinkedIn" — instead of the button staying stuck on "Connect LinkedIn" with no error.

cs_action.note: Automatic fix; nothing to enable. The broken connect affected all Advocacy recipients since approximately 2026-10-27 in US production.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer or speaker reports that clicking Connect LinkedIn does nothing, or that the button never changes after signing in to LinkedIn.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy clip share pages, Post to LinkedIn cards, or speaker verification — effectively all Advocacy users.
internal.gotchas: Sites learner connections (portal kind) still use the old opener path and will fail the same way if LinkedIn shows its sign-in page — a follow-up fix is planned.
internal.talk_track: LinkedIn changed a security header on their sign-in pages that broke the pop-up handshake. The fix routes the authorisation through a BroadcastChannel so the connect completes regardless of whether the pop-up can still talk to the opener.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that connecting LinkedIn opens a pop-up and that cancelling or declining on LinkedIn's consent screen shows a cancellation message on the card page.

entries.title: Sites in 29 languages, right to left for Arabic and Hebrew
entries.summary: Sites, submission forms and review portals now come in 29 languages, adding Portuguese (Brazil), Italian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Czech, Romanian, Hungarian, Greek, Ukrainian, Hindi and Malay to English, French, Spanish and German. A Site opens in the visitor's browser language, and Arabic and Hebrew read right to left.

where.path: Site → language menu

entries.use_case: Reviewers, speakers and applicants can use a Site in their own language instead of relying on browser translation.

cs_action.note: On for everyone; languages appear in the existing menus.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs events or programs with attendees, reviewers or speakers outside English, French, Spanish and German, especially APAC, Brazil, the Middle East and the Nordics.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with international reviewers, speakers, applicants or attendees.
internal.staff_path: Site → language menu

entries.title: The admin app, emails and Advocacy in 29 languages
entries.summary: The admin app, portals, Advocacy campaigns and cards, badges, wallet passes, sign-up and Sessionboard emails now offer Portuguese (Brazil), Italian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Czech, Romanian, Hungarian, Greek, Ukrainian, Hindi and Malay as well as English, French, Spanish and German. Every language picker lists all 29.

where.path: Language pickers across the app

entries.use_case: Teams and attendees outside the four original languages get the product, its emails and their share cards in their own language.

cs_action.note: On for everyone; languages appear in the existing menus.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs events or programs with attendees, reviewers or speakers outside English, French, Spanish and German, especially APAC, Brazil, the Middle East and the Nordics.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with international reviewers, speakers, applicants or attendees.
internal.staff_path: Language pickers across the app

entries.title: Embeds in 29 languages
entries.summary: Embedded widgets show their buttons, filters and empty states in any of 29 languages, following the page they sit on or the language attribute. Arabic and Hebrew embeds read right to left.

where.path: Embed language attribute

entries.use_case: Customers embedding Sessionboard on non-English websites get widgets that match their page.

cs_action.note: On for everyone; languages appear in the existing menus.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer runs events or programs with attendees, reviewers or speakers outside English, French, Spanish and German, especially APAC, Brazil, the Middle East and the Nordics.

entries.title: Home leads with a question: What do you want to happen?
entries.summary: Every event and organization now opens on **Home**. Say what you want to happen and the conversation opens full screen. Home also shows what the event is using and what to pick up next, and **All tools** lists every tool by the job it does.

where.path: Event sidebar → Home

entries.use_case: Teams start from the result they want instead of hunting through menus, and see at a glance which tools the event already uses and which their plan includes but they have not set up.

cs_action.note: On for everyone; nothing to turn on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks where the Dashboard or Your toolkit went, or why Ask no longer opens by itself.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Platform customer.
internal.staff_path: Event sidebar → Home (Dashboard is the row under it); Organization sidebar → Home
internal.gotchas: The Dashboard did not go away: it is the row directly under Home, with its tabs unchanged. Your toolkit is now the All tools tab on Home. Ask no longer opens as a side panel on arrival; the Ask button still opens it. Reviewer-only members land where they did before.
internal.talk_track: Home now starts with one question. Type what you want done and Ask takes it from there, full screen. Your dashboard is one row down, exactly as it was.

entries.title: New sign-ups land on a holding screen until staff grant access
entries.summary: After completing sign-up for a self-serve product, users who are placed on an access hold see a **"Thanks, you're on the list"** holding screen instead of entering the product. Any later sign-in attempt while the hold is active returns the same screen. Staff can review held accounts and click **Grant access** in the **Waiting for access** section of the self-serve funnel admin page.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the self-serve access hold; then /admin/self-serve-funnel → Waiting for access

where.path: /signup/hold (holding screen for new sign-ups) and /admin/self-serve-funnel → Waiting for access (staff grant)

entries.use_case: When Sessionboard wants to review new self-serve sign-ups before granting product access, the holding screen keeps users in a clear waiting state and staff can grant access one row at a time from the funnel admin page — no manual token work or support tickets needed.

cs_action.note: The access hold is a staff-controlled feature toggled at the API level. CS must coordinate with engineering to enable it for a product; the staff grant UI is at /admin/self-serve-funnel.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When the team is rolling out a new self-serve product and wants a manual approval step before users get in.
internal.who_should_get_it: Internal Sessionboard staff managing self-serve product launches that require a controlled rollout.
internal.staff_path: /admin/self-serve-funnel → Waiting for access
internal.gotchas: The ?new=1 bypass in the sign-up URL lets staff test the full sign-up flow without hitting the hold. The holding screen is public and requires no authentication. A 403 with code access_held on any API call also drops the user's tokens and redirects them to the holding screen.
internal.talk_track: If a new sign-up contacts support saying they finished sign-up but can't get in, check /admin/self-serve-funnel — they are likely in the Waiting for access queue and just need a Grant access click.

draft.docs_gap: The Early Access guide does not cover the self-serve access hold flow; a new section or guide should explain what the holding screen means for users and how staff grant access from the funnel admin page.
draft.why_use_it: The access hold gives Sessionboard staff a controlled gate between sign-up and first use of a self-serve product. New sign-ups receive a clear, branded confirmation that their request is received, while staff review each account and grant access when ready. The flow works across all sign-in methods — email code, magic link, Google and Microsoft — so no one slips through to the product before approval.

entries.title: Free-batch notices on reviewer invite and contact campaign send screens
entries.summary: When a free-trial batch is running low or exhausted, send screens in Awards (invite reviewers) and Marketing (contact campaign **Notify** dialog) now show how many invitations remain in the batch and how many would be left out. If more recipients are chosen than the batch allows, two explicit choices appear: **Invite the first N now** or **Add a card and invite all M**. After sending, the confirmation states what went out and what remains. The **Billing** page for both Awards and Marketing shows the remaining batch count per product.

where.path: Awards → Review → Reviewers (invite dialog) · Marketing → Campaigns → Notify dialog · Awards Billing · Marketing Billing

entries.use_case: Trial customers who are approaching or have hit their free send limit will never experience a silent partial send. They see exactly how many invitations remain, can choose to send within the batch now, or add a card to send to everyone at once — keeping them in control and reducing support tickets about missing invitations.

cs_action.note: Notices only appear when the free batch is nearly exhausted or used up and no card is on file. Customers with a card on file see no change. The underlying batch rule ships in web-api #5609; both PRs must be live for the notices to appear.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a trial customer asks why some reviewers or campaign recipients did not receive an invitation, or when a trial customer is approaching their send limit.
internal.who_should_get_it: All trial customers using Awards reviewer invites or Marketing contact campaigns who have not yet added a payment card.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Review → Reviewers → Invite · Marketing → Campaigns → Notify · Awards Billing · Marketing Billing
internal.gotchas: The Marketing campaign draft still shows the API refusal message with numbers but has no dedicated notice yet. The Awards reviewer file import also has no notice — a file larger than the remaining batch triggers the Add a card dialog instead. Learning and live captions are not covered in this batch.
internal.talk_track: During your trial you get a free batch of sends. When you get close to the limit, the invite and notify screens will tell you exactly how many are left and give you the choice to send within the batch now or add a card to send to everyone. Nothing goes out silently.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a section explaining the free-batch limit, what the notices look like on the invite and notify screens, the two choices when the batch is exceeded, and where to find the remaining count on the Billing page.
draft.why_use_it: The free-batch notices give trial organizers full visibility into how many sends remain before a card is required. Rather than silently dropping recipients, the platform surfaces the shortfall at the moment of sending and offers a clear path forward — send within the batch or add a card to cover everyone. The Billing page shows the remaining batch count for each product so organizers always know where they stand.

entries.title: Paste or upload last year's categories and criteria (Awards) or a question bank (Learning) during sign-up
entries.summary: During the **Awards** sign-up flow (`/signup/awards`), the **"What are you awarding?"** step now accepts a paste or file (text, CSV, Word .docx, PDF) containing last year's categories and judging criteria — the draft program preview shows the category names and a scorecard built from those criteria. During the **Learning** sign-up flow (`/signup/learning`), the **"first course"** step now accepts a question bank in GIFT, Aiken or CSV format — the preview shows how many questions were read and the first three. After the account is created, Awards programs are created with up to 50 categories and a scorecard of up to 12 criteria; Learning question banks are imported through the existing bank importer.

where.path: Sign-up → Awards (/signup/awards) or Learning (/signup/learning)

entries.use_case: An organizer signing up for Awards or Learning can bring in their existing materials — last year's award categories and judging criteria, or an existing question bank — before they even create an account, so their first program or course is pre-populated with real content rather than placeholder data.

cs_action.note: Default-on at sign-up; no configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or new customer mentions they are migrating from another awards or LMS platform and already have categories, criteria, or question banks they want to reuse.
internal.who_should_get_it: New sign-ups for Sessionboard Awards or Sessionboard Learning who have existing program materials.
internal.staff_path: /signup/awards or /signup/learning
internal.gotchas: File parsing is browser-side only; files are not uploaded to any server before account creation. Awards carries up to 50 categories and 12 scorecard criteria; Learning carries up to 40 KB of the bank (cut at a whole question) — the preview and post-import messaging tell the user when additional questions must be imported inside the product. PDF support is limited to 40 pages; Word files are unpacked up to 8 MB. Learning accepts text and CSV only (not Word or PDF). Binary files renamed to .txt are refused.
internal.talk_track: When you sign up for Awards or Learning, you can paste or upload your existing categories, criteria, or question bank right in the sign-up flow — before you even create an account. Your first program or course is built from your real content, not a blank template.

draft.docs_gap: The get-started guides for Awards and Learning should document the file-upload step in the sign-up conversation, including supported formats, size limits, and what is pre-populated in the first program or question bank after account creation.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Awards and Learning let you go from sign-up to a working program or course in minutes. Bringing in what you already have — award categories, scoring criteria, or a question bank — means your first draft reflects your real program rather than generic starter content. Awards builds the category list and scorecard from your file; Learning imports your questions directly into the bank so they are ready to add to any course.

entries.title: Bring a captions glossary when signing up for Sessionboard Marketing
entries.summary: During sign-up, a new **Words to spell right** step lets you paste or upload the names, product terms and acronyms that live captions should spell correctly. After the account is created, those words are pre-loaded into **Words to spell right** when you open Live Captions for the first time.

where.path: Sign-up → Words to spell right step (reached via /signup/marketing?bring=glossary)

entries.use_case: When a prospect already knows which product names or acronyms their captions get wrong, they can hand those terms over at sign-up so captions are accurate from the very first session — no manual entry after the workspace opens.

cs_action.note: The sign-up step is only reachable via the allow-listed URL parameter ?bring=glossary. Share that link with prospects who mention captions accuracy as a pain point.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or new customer mentions that live captions mis-spell their brand names, speaker names or technical terms.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer or prospect planning to use Live Captions who has a known list of terms to spell correctly.
internal.staff_path: /signup/marketing?bring=glossary — the Words to spell right step appears after the event is identified and before the preview.
internal.gotchas: The step is only accessible via ?bring=glossary; it does not appear on the standard sign-up flow. Words are carried in localStorage for that browser only — a person who finishes sign-up on a different device will need to paste the words again in Live Captions. The captions engine reads the first 100 terms; the UI warns when more than 100 are supplied. Terms longer than 60 characters or containing more than six words are silently dropped.
internal.talk_track: If you already have a list of product names or acronyms that trip up auto-captions, you can paste them right at sign-up and they will be waiting in Live Captions when you run your first session.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Words to spell right glossary feature in Live Captions: how to add terms, the 100-term limit that is sent per session, and how terms supplied at sign-up are pre-loaded into the first workspace.
draft.why_use_it: Live captions are more useful when they spell your organisation's specific names, acronyms and product terms correctly. The **Words to spell right** glossary lets you supply those terms once; they are sent to the captions engine each time a session starts, so every room benefits without any per-session setup.
